rejected_candidates.reason: The paper explicitly attributes their proofs to earlier work, so they do not provide self-contained source proof material for new tasks.

The compiled library has no scaled relative eigenvalue or eigenvector perturbation theorem corresponding to these results. Their generic spectral ingredients are Mathlib-level adapters, so they do not qualify as T1 or T2; Proposition 6.2 provides a broader self-contained T3 task.
The paper states that their proofs are omitted or analogous, so the source text is insufficient for a standalone proof task under the source-faithfulness rule.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Theorem 3.1, the detailed one-step floating-point two-sided Jacobi analysis
rejected_candidates.reason: This is a viable hard no-shortcut candidate, but Proposition 6.2 gives a cleaner fully source-proved T3 whose lack of a NumStability counterpart is unambiguous. The compiled Givens results use a different arithmetic model and do not establish Theorem 3.1's scaled symmetric commuting diagram.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Section 4 one-sided Jacobi results and Lemma 4.5
rejected_candidates.reason: The paper refers the detailed proofs to a technical report or earlier source, and the displayed conclusions do not supply the missing derivations.
Their detailed extension proofs are referred to earlier reports, and the available compiled QR modules do not prove the paper-specific Jacobi accuracy claims.

Both have proofs, but Proposition 6.1 alone is narrower and Proposition 6.3 builds on Proposition 6.2. Retaining all five parts of Proposition 6.2 gives the direct self-contained Hadamard-measure result at the required difficulty.

rejected_candidates.candidate: Section 7 experiments and Section 8 open questions
rejected_candidates.reason: The former are empirical observations and the latter are explicitly unresolved rather than proved universal claims.

T1.decision: Skipped. The compatible importable set has no one substantial result that materially shortens a source-proved P35 theorem. Conventional Givens application uses a different addition model from equation (3.1), and the spectral adapters do not provide the paper's scaled perturbation conclusions.

T2.decision: Skipped. No source proof requires at least two distinct substantial compatible results from the compiled library. Combining conventional Givens and generic spectral facts would remain insufficient for the two-sided scaled Jacobi analysis and would manufacture a dependency not present in the source proof.

T3.decision: Selected all five parts of Proposition 6.2. The task retains the equality characterization, diagonal scaling, eigenvalue-product bound, exact Jacobi update, and finite-run condition-growth result, while neither Mathlib nor NumStability supplies a corresponding theorem.

selection_policy: Use only conclusions whose statements and supporting derivations are present in this paper.
Do not turn results whose detailed proofs are referred to earlier papers or reports into tasks.
Do not count compiled conventional Givens results as corresponding to the paper's different no-guard-digit arithmetic model.
Retain all five parts of Proposition 6.2 rather than extracting only its Mathlib-supported AM-GM substep.
Keep every public definition paper-scoped and free of NumStability imports.
Assign tiers only after comparison with the complete frozen NumStability source, its importable compiled subset, and Mathlib.
